title: The locale is a query parameter
lead: Every page keeps one URL. The locale rides in the query string, the server reads it before rendering, and the language switcher is an ordinary link.

shareable.title: Shareable
shareable.text: A link carries its language: /about?lang=cs opens in Czech for whoever receives it.

server.title: Resolved on the server
server.text: The page is rendered in the requested language, so there is no flash of the wrong one.

unknown.title: Unknown values fall back
unknown.text: ?lang= is visitor-controlled. Anything outside the configured set is dropped, never handed to the instance.

note.title: Not the SEO option
note.text: Search engines treat a query parameter as the same page. If the language should be part of the address, look at locale-router instead.
